newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Wesfarmers says no capital raising.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Wesfarmers says no capital raising.

text.p: Diversified industrial group Wesfarmers Ltd said on Tuesday it did not expect that it would have to raise any more capital over the next year as its gearing had improved above expectations to about 42 percent in the first four months of the 1996/97 year.
Wesfarmers chief executive Michael Chaney said the gearing ratio was expected to fall further over the coming year and was well within Wesfarmer's targeted 40 to 65 percent range.
This left room for Wesfarmers to borrow about A$200 million, he said.
However, Wesfarmers would have no hesitation in going to market to raise new equity if a large acquisition opportunity came along, but it had no such plans at the moment, he said.
"We've had a view that we've never been constrained with respect to capital," Chaney told reporters after a Securities Institute of Australia briefing.
"That is if we managed to find investments that were worthwhile, the market would be happy to fund them," he said.

"So if it was a large acquisition and it would blow out our gearing ratio, we'd just go to the market. But given our current plans and all our expenditures, we don't have any expectation of doing that."
